name: Model Behavior Lab
promise: Produce reproducible, evidence-linked model capability profiles.
completion_criteria: Every run pins benchmark, scorer, provider, model, request parameters, and iteration policy.
Raw evidence, structured results, cost, errors, retries, and partial completion remain linked.
Ethics and chess behaviors are packs/adapters over one run/report kernel.
Collaborator-owned sources remain externally owned and are changed or republished only by agreement.

waves.objective: Map one ethics scenario and result into ExperimentRun.
waves.acceptance: The original and normalized result match on prompt, response, score, metadata, and failures.
waves.runtime_followup: Re-run the donor experiment runner live instead of normalizing a stored result file.

waves.objective: Measure the duplicated subsystems that an ethics benchmark-pack extraction would replace.
waves.acceptance: The extraction matrix names both donor corpora and every measured duplicate subsystem while recording that no canonical slice was implemented and no runtime was removed.
waves.runtime_followup: Implement the shared slice and delete the duplicated donor subsystems; this gate only measures them.

waves.objective: Build a recorded-opening chess fixture from real donor match logs and exercise the suite-local legality checker against it.
waves.acceptance: The first recorded ply receives a stable legality verdict from the suite-local checker, and the receipt states that the donor legality checker was not invoked and that a whole match was not replayed or advanced.
waves.runtime_followup: Replay a whole recorded match once the engine can apply moves, rather than validating opening ply.

waves.objective: Extract second benchmark pack (chess legal moves and tactics) over comparator kernel.
waves.acceptance: Deterministic chess scoring rules verify kernel generality across disparate benchmark domains.
waves.runtime_followup: Score full match transcripts and tactical puzzles, not the first ply of each match.

waves.objective: Define a content-pinned corpus manifest for the retained ethics and chess inputs.
waves.acceptance: Every listed retained input is content-addressed and source-fingerprinted; an end-to-end historical or live re-run remains a runtime follow-up.
waves.runtime_followup: Prove the manifest re-runs a historical evaluation end to end from its pinned hashes.
